tax.text: Garrett says he will fight to lower taxes and extend the 2017 tax cuts.
tax.quote: That’s why he will always fight to lower taxes and ensure that President Trump’s 2017 tax cuts are not only permanent, but also expand them further to keep more money in your own pocket, not the government’s.

debt.text: He says the federal government should balance its budget as Tennessee does.
debt.quote: Johnny believes that if Tennessee families and the State have to balance their budget, the federal government should too.

schools.text: He voted for legislation increasing the maximum number of education freedom scholarships from 25,000 to 35,000.
schools.quote: Representatives voting Aye were: Baum, Boyd, Bulso, Butler, Capley, Carringer, Cepicky, Crawford, Davis, Doggett, Eldridge, Faison, Farmer, Gant, Garrett, Gillespie, Grills, Hale, Helton-Haynes, Hicks T, Hill, Hulsey, Kumar, Lafferty, Lamberth, Lankford, Leatherwood, Littleton, Lynn, Maberry, Marsh, Martin B, Martin G, McCalmon, Moody, Powers, Reedy, Reeves, Rudd, Rudder, Slater, Sparks, Stevens, Terry, Todd, Vaughan, Vital, White, Williams, Wright, Zachary, Mr. Speaker Sexton -- 52.

safety.text: Garrett says he has advocated for law enforcement and led legislation to classify murdering a police officer as a terrorist crime.
safety.quote: He led the fight to pass legislation that classifies murdering a police officer as a terrorist crime.

immigration.text: Garrett supports working with ICE to deport undocumented immigrants and says a border wall is necessary.
immigration.quote: That’s why Johnny took action in the Tennessee House to implement a State Border Czar who will work hand in glove with ICE to deport all illegal aliens from the Volunteer State.

guns.text: Garrett says he will fight to defend Americans’ right to bear arms.
guns.quote: Every American has the Constitutional right to bear arms, and as your Congressman, he’ll always fight for that right.

abortion.text: Garrett calls himself 100% pro-life, says life begins at conception, and pledges to advocate for the unborn.
abortion.quote: Johnny is 100% Pro-Life. He believes that life begins at conception, and he will always fight as a voice for the voiceless.

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: Garrett says he passed legislation barring men from competing in women’s sports and will continue to support that policy.
gender.quote: As State Representative, Johnny passed legislation banning men from competing in women’s sports and will continue to stand up for common sense in Washington to protect women’s sports.

energy.text: He supports domestic energy infrastructure for AI systems while saying it should not burden consumers.
energy.quote: supporting strong domestic energy infrastructure to power AI systems without burdening consumers

tax.text: He supports requiring wealthy people to pay more and reversing cuts to programs families use.
tax.quote: Mike believes in ending broad tariffs, reversing federal cuts to programs that families depend on, requiring the wealthy to pay a fair share, expanding affordable housing, and strengthening labor standards, for starters.

wages.text: Croley supports raising the minimum wage, strengthening labor standards, and making it easier for workers to unionize.
wages.quote: Mike supports fair wages, strong labor standards, and making it easier for workers to unionize. Mike also supports raising the minimum wage to a fair wage.

trade.text: Croley says he supports ending broad tariffs.
trade.quote: Mike believes in ending broad tariffs, reversing federal cuts to programs that families depend on, requiring the wealthy to pay a fair share, expanding affordable housing, and strengthening labor standards, for starters.

debt.text: Croley supports protecting Social Security and opposes cuts to earned benefits.
debt.quote: Mike supports protecting Social Security and opposes cuts to earned benefits.

housing.text: Croley supports building quality, affordable housing and limiting corporate purchases of family homes.
housing.quote: Mike supports building quality, affordable housing and limiting corporations from buying large numbers of family homes.

schools.text: Croley supports increasing school funding and ending the voucher program.
schools.quote: Mike supports increasing school funding, doing away with the voucher program, increasing teacher pay, and protecting students with disabilities.

immigration.text: Croley supports scaling back DHS and ICE funding to require reforms and says immigration enforcement must respect due process and human rights.
immigration.quote: Due process matters. The Constitution matters. Enforcing immigration law should never come at the expense of basic human rights.

guns.text: Croley supports universal background checks for gun purchases while saying he does not support confiscation.
guns.quote: I support Universal Background Checks because I believe in the same vetting for the public that I was held to as an officer.

cannabis.text: Croley supports federal recreational marijuana legalization with regulation and taxation.
cannabis.quote: It is past time that we legalize recreational marijuana at the federal level.

health.text: Croley supports extending the Affordable Care Act and opposes cuts to Medicaid and Medicare.
health.quote: Mike supports extending the Affordable Care Act and opposes cuts to Medicaid and Medicare.

voting.text: He supports making voting more accessible and expanding participation.
voting.quote: Mike believes in making voting more accessible, protecting voting rights, and expanding participation.

guns.text: In a candidate questionnaire, he said no gun ownership restrictions were needed, while allowing an exception for some felons after probation.
guns.quote: None, it is the right of every person to defend themselves. However, felons should be able to purchase firearms after the set time of probation has been met.

wages.text: He said he wants working-class Nashvillians paid a living wage, starting with Metro employees.
wages.quote: I want to ensure working-class Nashvillians are paid a living wage. This starts with Metro employees.

housing.text: His Metro Council campaign said building affordable housing was part of its community-building agenda.
housing.quote: Part of building a city-wide sense of community means connecting more of our neighborhoods together, improving mass transit, prioritizing pedestrian and bicyclist safety, building affordable housing, and enforcing restrictions on short term rentals owned by outside investors.

safety.text: He described himself as an abolitionist and said he favors preventive approaches to crime reduction.
safety.quote: I'm an abolitionist. While police and prison abolition doesn't resonate in a district as affluent as mine, I've been transparent with my neighbors about my desire to seek preventative rather than reactive measures when approaching crime reduction in Nashville.
